summary: Log-cabin lookout on a 9,349-ft peak in the River of No Return Wilderness; listed destroyed in 1965, though the sources disagree on its dates.

facts.status_note: Listed as destroyed in 1965; a 1982 history says very little, if anything, remains on the summit

visit.trail_note: Hike-in only, deep in the River of No Return Wilderness; reached by packing in from the Salmon River Lodge or landing at the Cold Meadows airstrip

The 1935 map still calls it a lookout station (Bing Young, 1982)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Idaho County Cottonwood Butte near Craigmont (1952 cabin, gone by 1994) is a different peak. Its 1955 Air Force communications site and radio station do not belong to this record.

sources.title: Cottonwood Butte 9349, quoting Bing Young, Salmon National Forest Fire Lookouts (1982)

notes_for_editor: Dates conflict. firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts both give 1965 and may not be independent. Bing Young (1982, via the climbing guide) doubts the cabin lasted long after the 1935 map. Idaho Fire Lookouts lists Don Clark for 1987-1989, which is after its own 1965 date. WillhiteWeb says the Idaho County Cottonwood Butte was still staffed in 1989, so that entry may be a mix-up; not confirmed. Do not merge with the Idaho County Cottonwood Butte near Craigmont (1952 cabin, gone by 1994). A search snippet also mentions a 1965 radar station dismantling on a Cottonwood Butte (St Gertrude's Museum Facebook post, not fetched); it appears to concern the Idaho County peak. Access level left unset: sources describe wilderness and foot access but no public-access status. The record has no build year; the 1920 event year is a placeholder for the decade. No new photos.
